players.product: intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157) individualized neoantigen therapy, jointly developed with Merck

quarterly_data.signal: Chief Development Officer David Berman on the intismeran phase III adjuvant melanoma trial (intismeran plus KEYTRUDA versus KEYTRUDA): it hit its primary endpoint at the first interim analysis and also hit the secondary endpoint, distant metastasis-free survival, at that interim; he called it the first adjuvant trial to hit both primary and secondary endpoints at the interim and the first phase III adjuvant trial to beat a PD-1 monotherapy as an add-on (company claims). The trial combined stage II and stage III patients in one population and is an 1,100-patient, rigorously controlled, blinded phase III; Berman: 'I am very confident that we have a strong case for approval.' CEO Stephane Bancel: the company is focusing on filing the BLA as fast as it can.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,100-patient blinded phase III; primary endpoint and distant metastasis-free survival met at the first interim analysis

quarterly_data.signal: Berman on the wider intismeran program: screening has stopped on the leading phase III adjuvant lung cancer trial in patients with no prior neoadjuvant therapy, with randomization expected to be complete later this year (posted on ClinicalTrials.gov); the three lung phase IIIs include a stage 1 lung cancer phase III, and a randomized phase II in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with BCG is ongoing. Kidney (RCC) and bladder cancer studies should read out hopefully over the next 12 months or so; the company is also studying metastatic disease, pancreatic cancer and gastric cancer. Each individualized cassette codes 34 neoantigens, of which usually about one-third are immunogenic; Berman believes intismeran does not need a PD-1 to be active. Bancel: with Merck the company is looking at how to accelerate new studies beyond the 9 ongoing.
quarterly_data.figure: leading adjuvant lung phase III randomization expected complete later this year; RCC and bladder readouts over the next 12 months or so; 34 neoantigens per cassette

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline beyond intismeran: Berman - the off-the-shelf Lynch syndrome neoantigen vaccine is in an ongoing phase I/II trial in the U.K. aimed at cancer interception (CEO Stephane Bancel: University of Oxford is involved, Moderna owns the program 100%, Lynch syndrome affects 1 in 400 people and a product could be offered through retail pharmacies); off-the-shelf shared-antigen cancer vaccines are in phase I; the multiplexed T-cell engager phase I in heavily pretreated multiple myeloma (three T-cell engagers in one drug, which he called a first) is progressing well, with data to be shared later this year. Bancel: the in vivo CAR T program for autoimmune disease is heading to the clinic, with progress on autoimmune programs to be shared over the next 12 to 18 months.
quarterly_data.figure: multiple myeloma T-cell engager data later this year; autoimmune program updates over the next 12 to 18 months

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephane Bancel: the vaccine business has five approved products with two products launching this year. Rare liver diseases beyond propionic acidemia (PA) use the same lipid and the same manufacturing as PA, and the company has published more than 12 models of rare genetic liver disease; he expects great PA pivotal data, consistent with the phase I/II results. Today cost of goods 'do not look great' because the seasonal vaccine factories do nothing for half of the year, and loading them off-season with rare disease products would leverage fixed cost. He views Moderna as the only mRNA platform company left (citing CureVac gone, BioNTech splitting the company and Sanofi stopping its mRNA vaccine programs).
quarterly_data.figure: five approved vaccine products, two launching this year; more than 12 rare liver disease models published

connects_to.relationship: PCV collaboration and license agreement for intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157): Moderna designs and manufactures intismeran and provides manufacturing capacity

contracts.signal: CEO Stephane Bancel: the intismeran collaboration with Merck works as a virtual JV (no legal JV) - 50-50 cost in for everything, including sales reps, clinical studies, manufacturing, capex and opex, with 50% of the profit going to each company. All proprietary neoantigen-selection information stays within Moderna (partners supply the sequencing raw data). Moderna and Merck are setting up joint teams to prepare hospitals one by one for launch, which he sees as the biggest bottleneck rather than manufacturing.
